content: Hey everyone, I'm following along the Lean functional programming tutorial and found that when I write a definition like def fourAndThree : Point :=, the vscode plugin doesn't automatically put in the tab indentation for the definition body after I press Enter. Is there a reason why this is the case like some syntactical reason that I haven't encountered yet?... I'm new to this. Cheers!
This topic was moved here from #lean4 > vscode-lean4 Enter auto-indentation by Kevin Buzzard.

AFAIK auto-indentation isn't a solved problem in general, but perhaps for simple cases it could work.
I believe this is the config you could try tweaking, perhaps it could use some := or by.

There was a previous good attempt at this by @Thomas Murrills at vscode-lean4#329.
Ultimately, using static regexes to decide when to add indentation is just too fragile in a super extensible language like Lean, and we decided that consistently adding no indentation will be far less annoying than sometimes adding indentation and sometimes getting it wrong.

There's an LSP request for this as well that would be less brittle, but we can't always respond to it with latency that is so low that it doesn't become annoying while typing (Lean sometimes needs to elaborate commands in order to continue parsing!).
